newsitem.title: UK: Barclays says Q1 marks good start to year.
newsitem.headline: Barclays says Q1 marks good start to year.

text.p: British banking giant Barclays Plc said on Tuesday it made a good start to 1997, with an encouraging first quarter for its investment banking arm, BZW.

"BZW had an encouraging first quarter, despite the fact that the trading environment has recently become more subdued," chairman Andrew Buxton said in a statement from Barclay's annual general meeting.
Barclays says Q1 marks good start to =2
Buxton said Barclays' personal and business banking continued to post a strong performance.
"In business banking in particular, provisions remain at a low level, a reflection of economic conditions and the prudent management of our book," he said.
Barclays' shares firmed 9.5 pence to 1038 pence by 1115 GMT.

Barclays planned to continue investing in customer service and cost efficiency improvements, particularly in its personal banking business and in BZW, after investing a total of about 800 million pounds ($1.3 billion) toward that end in 1996.
Buxton also said Barclays would continue to return to shareholders capital that was not required for the development of its business.
The bank returned 290 million pounds of capital to shareholders earlier this year in addition to its buyback of roughly 780 million pounds worth of shares in 1996.

In other matters, Buxton said Barclays was preparing for European Monetary Union on the assumption that EMU would come into effect on January 1, 1999, but that Britain would not likely be a member at that stage. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
